manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the bottle on the table and lift it.

Task description: The target is the white bottle lying horizontally on the table. Use the right gripper to pick it up and adjust it to a nearly upright pose with its cap facing up.

Success criteria: The bottle is grasped and lifted off the table, with its body nearly vertical, cap up and base down. Merely lifting it horizontally does not count.

## Execution tips

- Select straighter middle bottle sidewalls for grasping, closing opposite fingers perpendicular to the bottle's long axis. Avoid shoulders and rounded base edges to reduce off-center gripping or slipping.
- Open slightly wider than the selected grasp section. Before closing, confirm both fingers lie on opposite sides with effective pad contact, avoiding a grasp based only on image overlap or one finger pushing the bottle into a roll.
- When adjusting the bottle pose, leave enough clearance below the bottom for it to rotate downward. Make small pose adjustments to reduce contact between the bottom and table and slipping of the bottle body.
- Use both views to check the actual height relationship between the cap and base, avoiding mistaking a bottle that only appears upright in one view for a truly upright pose.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start the sole physical-robot episode with the specified parameters, operate from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.

The manual matches the scene: the white bottle lies horizontally with its cap left in the image. I am orienting the gripper above it to grip the body middle, then will gradually right it after secure grasping and lifting.

The gripper is still above the bottle and has not made contact. Live feedback shows the move is complete; I am rotating the gripper so its closing direction spans the bottle body and preserves joint range for the descent.

The gripper's closing direction is now approximately across the bottle, which remains in its original position on the table. Next I will descend gradually and use a close-up view to confirm both fingers are on opposite sides before closing.
The bottle body is between the open fingers, but not yet at grasp height. I will continue descending in steps no larger than 1 cm and correct gripper tilt to avoid one finger touching first.
In the close view, the fingers remain on opposite bottle sides and have not rolled it away. I am completing final downward alignment, then will close and make a small test lift to check security.

The bottle slipped during the test lift and fell back onto the table; the gripper opening returned close to its empty-grasp value. The episode can continue. I will reopen, lower the pads nearer the bottle-body center and regrasp.

This time I lowered the grasp height by about 1.8 cm, and the gripper is closer to pointing vertically downward. Once both fingers are aligned against the bottle's side wall, I will close again and check for slipping during a test lift.

During the second test lift, the bottle left the table with the gripper and the opening remained stable without visible slipping. I have begun small-angle orientation adjustments and will rotate the cap upward while maintaining bottle-bottom clearance and wrist-joint margin.

The bottle remains held, and its cap end has started to rise. To avoid approaching the wrist-joint limit, I will continue lifting while adjusting its horizontal direction in stages, then finish turning it upright.

The bottle has been raised higher, with the grasp opening still about 63 mm. Next I will continue turning it upright. The arm partly obscures the bottle, so after adjustment I must check the cap and bottom positions using both views.
The grasp remains stable and the bottle is gradually approaching upright. A few final small-angle adjustments and a clearer side view are needed to judge whether the cap is up and bottom down.

The last pose adjustment was rejected by the controller's orientation-angle range check, and feedback shows it was not executed. The bottle remains grasped. I will reduce the adjustment angle based on the current state, then recheck the hold.

After waiting and rechecking, the gripper opening remains about 63 mm, with no further bottle sliding observed. From the grasp direction and live pose, I judge that the bottle is lifted and nearly upright with its cap up. The final image is occluded, so an on-site operator must still confirm. I will now end this episode.
